title: Algebraic Manipulation
description: Collecting like terms, expanding single and double brackets, factorising linear and simple quadratic expressions, and simplifying algebraic fractions.

notes.heading: Terms, Coefficients and Constants
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An **algebraic term** is a number, a letter, or a number multiplied by a letter, such as $3x$, $-5y$, $x^2$ or $12$. The **coefficient** of a term is the number multiplying the letter, including its sign.

🔑 How it works
An expression is split into terms by the + and − signs between them, and each sign belongs to the term that follows it. So $6x - 2x + 8$ has three terms: $6x$, $-2x$ and $8$.

💡 Worked Example
In the expression $9x^2 - 4x + 1$, the coefficient of $x^2$ is $9$, the coefficient of $x$ is $-4$, and $1$ is called the **constant term** because it contains no letter.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Thinking that a lone letter has no coefficient. The term $x$ means $1x$, and $-x$ means $-1x$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A term is a number, a letter, or a product of numbers and letters.
• Coefficients carry their sign: in $7 - 2x$ the coefficient of $x$ is $-2$.
• A number on its own is the constant term.

notes.heading: Collecting Like Terms
notes.body:
📌 Definition
**Like terms** have exactly the same letters with exactly the same powers — only their coefficients may differ. $5x$ and $-2x$ are like terms; $5x$ and $5x^2$ are not.

🔑 How it works
To collect like terms, add or subtract the coefficients and keep the letter part unchanged. Unlike terms simply stay where they are: $3x + 4y$ cannot be simplified further.

💡 Worked Example 1
Simplify $7x + 3 - 2x + 8$.

The like pairs are $7x$ with $-2x$, and $3$ with $8$.

$7x - 2x = 5x$ and $3 + 8 = 11$, so the answer is $5x + 11$.

💡 Worked Example 2
Simplify $4a + 6b - a - 2b$.

$4a - a = 3a$ and $6b - 2b = 4b$, so the answer is $3a + 4b$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Combining terms that are not alike. $x + x^2$ does **not** equal $2x^2$, and $3x + 3y$ does **not** equal $3xy$. Adding different powers never changes the power.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Only like terms can be collected.
• $x - 2x = -x$, not $0$ and not $x$.
• A tidy final answer lists terms in descending power order.

notes.heading: Expanding a Single Bracket
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To **expand** a bracket means to multiply everything inside the bracket by the term outside it.

🔑 How it works
The multiplier outside applies to every term inside, and its sign applies too:

$$a(b + c) = ab + ac$$

💡 Worked Example 1
Expand $3(x + 5)$.

$3 \times x + 3 \times 5 = 3x + 15$

💡 Worked Example 2
Expand $-2(x - 4)$.

$-2 \times x + (-2) \times (-4) = -2x + 8$

💡 Worked Example 3
Expand $x(2x + 7)$.

$x \times 2x + x \times 7 = 2x^2 + 7x$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Multiplying only the first term inside, or getting the final sign wrong when the outside term is negative. In $-2(x - 4)$ the constant is $+8$, not $-8$, because a negative times a negative is positive.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Brackets hide more than one term — multiply them all.
• A negative multiplier flips every sign inside.
• Expanding and factorising are inverse operations: expand your answer back to check it.

notes.heading: Expanding Double Brackets
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To expand $(a+b)(c+d)$, every term of the first bracket multiplies every term of the second bracket.

🔑 How it works
For two brackets each of the form $(x + \text{number})$ there is a quick pattern — the middle coefficient is the **sum** of the numbers and the constant is their **product**:

$$(x + p)(x + q) = x^2 + (p+q)x + pq$$

💡 Worked Example 1
Expand $(x + 4)(x + 3)$.

$x^2 + 3x + 4x + 12 = x^2 + 7x + 12$

💡 Worked Example 2
Expand $(2x - 5)(x + 2)$.

$2x^2 + 4x - 5x - 10 = 2x^2 - x - 10$

💡 Worked Example 3 — difference of two squares
Expand $(x + 6)(x - 6)$.

$x^2 - 6x + 6x - 36 = x^2 - 36$ — the middle terms always cancel.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Missing one of the four products. A reliable check: before collecting, expanding two brackets always produces four terms.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $(x+p)(x+q) = x^2 + (p+q)x + pq$.
• $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$ has no middle term.
• Track signs carefully: $(-5) \times (+2)$ contributes $-10$.

notes.heading: Factorising with a Single Bracket
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To **factorise** an expression means to rewrite it as a product. With a single bracket, take the highest common factor (HCF) of all the terms outside.

🔑 How it works
1. Find the HCF of the coefficients.
2. Find the lowest power of each letter that appears in every term.
3. Divide each term by the HCF to find what remains inside the bracket.

💡 Worked Example 1
Factorise $6x + 9$.

The HCF of $6$ and $9$ is $3$, so $6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)$.

💡 Worked Example 2
Factorise $4x^2 + 8x$ fully.

The HCF is $4x$, so $4x^2 + 8x = 4x(x + 2)$.

💡 Worked Example 3
Factorise $15a^2b - 5ab^2$ fully.

The HCF is $5ab$, so $15a^2b - 5ab^2 = 5ab(3a - b)$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Stopping short of the highest common factor. Writing $6x^2 + 9x = 3(2x^2 + 3x)$ is correct but not **fully** factorised — the answer is $3x(2x + 3)$, because $x$ is also common.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• "Fully factorise" means nothing common is left inside the bracket.
• Always check by expanding back out.
• When a letter appears in every term, the lowest power of it goes outside.

notes.heading: Factorising Simple Quadratics
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A **quadratic expression** contains an $x^2$ term, such as $x^2 + 5x + 6$. Factorising one means writing it as a product of two brackets.

🔑 How it works
For $x^2 + bx + c$, find two numbers that multiply to give $c$ and add to give $b$:

$$x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x+p)(x+q)$$

💡 Worked Example 1
Factorise $x^2 + 7x + 12$.

Two numbers multiplying to $12$ and adding to $7$ are $3$ and $4$, so $x^2 + 7x + 12 = (x+3)(x+4)$.

💡 Worked Example 2
Factorise $x^2 - 2x - 8$.

Two numbers multiplying to $-8$ and adding to $-2$ are $-4$ and $+2$, so $x^2 - 2x - 8 = (x-4)(x+2)$.

💡 Worked Example 3 — difference of two squares
Factorise $x^2 - 25$.

A missing middle term means the two numbers are opposites: $x^2 - 25 = (x+5)(x-5)$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Sign slips when $c$ is negative: the two numbers must have opposite signs because their product is negative.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiply to $c$, add to $b$.
• If $c$ is positive, both numbers share the sign of $b$.
• $x^2 - k^2 = (x+k)(x-k)$ every time.

notes.heading: Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An **algebraic fraction** has algebra in its numerator or denominator, such as $\dfrac{8x}{2}$ or $\dfrac{6x^2}{3x}$.

🔑 How it works
Simplify by cancelling common **factors**, exactly as with ordinary fractions: divide the coefficients, and use the index law $x^m \div x^n = x^{m-n}$ for the letters.

💡 Worked Example 1
Simplify $\dfrac{14x}{7}$.

$14 \div 7 = 2$, so $\dfrac{14x}{7} = 2x$.

💡 Worked Example 2
Simplify $\dfrac{10x^3}{5x}$.

$10 \div 5 = 2$ and $x^3 \div x = x^2$, so the answer is $2x^2$.

💡 Worked Example 3
Simplify $\dfrac{12x^2 + 8x}{4x}$.

Factorise the numerator first: $\dfrac{4x(3x + 2)}{4x} = 3x + 2$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Cancelling terms instead of factors. In $\dfrac{6x + 3}{3}$ you may cancel the $3$ only after factorising: $\dfrac{3(2x+1)}{3} = 2x + 1$. The expression $\dfrac{x+2}{x}$ cannot be cancelled at all.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Only common factors cancel — never part of a sum.
• When in doubt, factorise the top (and bottom) first.
• Check by substituting a value, such as $x = 2$, into the original and the simplified version.

questions.explanation: Collect like terms: $5x - 2x = 3x$ and $3 + 9 = 12$, giving $3x + 12$. The $x$ terms and the numbers are collected separately.
Multiply both terms inside by $4$: $4 \times x = 4x$ and $4 \times (-7) = -28$, so the answer is $4x - 28$. Forgetting to multiply the second term gives the trap $4x - 7$.
Like terms have the same letter raised to the same power, so $7x^2$ and $-3x^2$ qualify. Different letters, different powers, and constants paired with $x$ terms are all unlike.
The HCF of $8$ and $12$ is $4$, so $8x + 12 = 4(2x + 3)$. The answer $2(4x + 6)$ is equal in value but not fully factorised, since $4x$ and $6$ still share a factor of $2$.
Collect the $x$ terms and the $y$ terms separately: $9x - 2x = 7x$ and $-4y + 6y = 2y$, giving $7x + 2y$. Each term carries its own sign when collecting.
Multiply each term by $-3x$: $-3x \times x = -3x^2$ and $-3x \times (-5) = +15x$, so the answer is $-3x^2 + 15x$. A negative times a negative gives the positive middle term.
Expanding fully: $x^2 - 2x + 7x - 14 = x^2 + 5x - 14$. The numbers multiply to $-14$ and add to $+5$, which is a quick way to check the answer.
All four products are needed: $3x^2 + 15x + 2x + 10$. Collecting the middle terms gives $15x + 2x = 17x$, so the answer is $3x^2 + 17x + 10$.
The HCF of $10x^2$ and $15x$ is $5x$ — both the coefficients and one power of $x$ are common — so the full factorisation is $5x(2x - 3)$. The other factorisations leave a common factor inside.
This is a difference of two squares: $x^2 - 7^2 = (x+7)(x-7)$. The middle term is missing because the $+7x$ and $-7x$ cancel when expanded.
Find two numbers multiplying to $20$ and adding to $9$: they are $4$ and $5$, so $x^2 + 9x + 20 = (x+4)(x+5)$. The option $(x-4)(x-5)$ expands to $x^2 - 9x + 20$ — right numbers, wrong signs.

The HCF of $12$ and $18$ is $6$, and the lowest power of $x$ common to both terms is $x^2$, so the full factorisation is $6x^2(2x - 3)$. Options like $3x^2(4x-6)$ still hide a common factor inside the bracket.
First part: $(x+4)(x-4) = x^2 - 16$ (difference of two squares). Second part: $2x(x+3) = 2x^2 + 6x$. Adding gives $x^2 - 16 + 2x^2 + 6x = 3x^2 + 6x - 16$.
Divide the coefficients: $16 \div 8 = 2$. Subtract the powers: $x^5 \div x^2 = x^{5-2} = x^3$. The answer is $2x^3$. Adding the powers instead of subtracting gives the trap $2x^8$.
$(2x-3)(x+4) = 2x^2 + 5x - 12$ and $x(2x-1) = 2x^2 - x$. Subtracting: $2x^2 + 5x - 12 - (2x^2 - x) = 2x^2 + 5x - 12 - 2x^2 + x = 6x - 12$. The $x^2$ terms cancel, and subtracting $-x$ adds $+x$.
